x: He means by His saying, may His praise be exalted, glorify God pray to God and prostrate to Him whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise He says: He is the Exalted in His vengeance upon those of His creation who took vengeance for their disobedience to Him, the Wise in His management of them.
He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering

, God is the One who expelled those who denied the Prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, from the People of the Scripture, and they were the Jews of Banu Nadir, from their homes. This was their expulsion from their homes and houses, when they made peace with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, on the condition that he would grant them security regarding their blood, women, and children, and that they would have whatever their camels carried of their wealth, leaving their homes and the rest of their wealth for him. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, agreed to that, so they left their homes, some of them went to Syria, and some of them went to Khaybar. This is what God, the Most High, said,
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering
, he said: Al-Nadir until His statement, and to disgrace the wicked. He mentioned all of that about them:

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering
. It was said: Ash-Sham, and they are Banu Nadir, a tribe of Jews, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled them from Medina to Khaybar, his return from Uhud.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: From their homes until the first gathering. He said: They are Banu al-Nadir. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought them until he made peace with them regarding exile. He exiled them to Syria on the condition that they would have whatever camels carried except weapons. The weapon is the ring. They were from a tribe that had not been exiled in the past, and God Almighty had decreed exile upon them. If it had not been for that, He would have punished them in this world with killing and captivity.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering
, he said: These were the Nadir when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, who said:
m: Surah al-Hashr was revealed in its entirety regarding Banu al-Nadir. It mentions what God Almighty afflicted them with of His vengeance, and what He empowered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with over them and what He did to them. He said,
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering
[the verses]. And His saying:
h
For the first gathering
, God Almighty says:
h
For the first gathering
in this world, and that is their gathering to the land of Ash-Sham. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement, at the first gathering, he said: Their exile was the first gathering in the world to the Levant.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us,
m: on the
h
It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering

. You did not think that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God. But God came upon them from where they had not expected and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, you who have vision! authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A fire will come from the east of the earth, and will gather the people to its west. It will spend the night with them where they spent the night, and will take their naps with them where they took their naps, and will consume whoever is left behind.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: It reached me that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled Banu Nadir, he said: Go on, for this is the first gathering, and we will follow in its footsteps.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
For the first gathering

, he said: Ash-Sham when He returned them to Ash-Sham, and he recited the statement of God Almighty, O you who have been given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming that which is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them on their backs
r
(An-Nisa’: 47)
. He said: From where their backs came, that is, they returned to Ash-Sham from where they came, they were returned to it. And His statement:
h
You did not think that they would leave means that God Almighty says to the believing companions of the Messenger of God

, may God bless him and grant him peace: You did not think that these people of the Book whom God expelled from their homes would leave their dwellings and homes, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God. Rather, the people thought, as mentioned, that Abdullah bin Ubayy and a group of hypocrites sent to them when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them, ordering them to remain in their fortresses and promising them victory.

c: Ibn Humayd also told me, saying: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman,
m: that a group of Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, including Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi’ah and Malik ibn Nawfal, Suwayd and Da’is, sent to Banu al-Nadir, saying: “Stand firm and resist, for we will not surrender you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you go out, we will go out with you.” So they waited for someone to help them, but they did not do so, and they had fortified themselves in the fortresses of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he descended upon them. And His statement,
h
So God came to them from where they had not expected

, God Almighty says: So God’s command came to them from where they had not expected it would come to them. And that command that came to them from God from where they had not expected was that He cast terror into their hearts because of the descent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among his companions. God Almighty says: And He cast terror into their hearts. And His saying:
h
They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers

means, may His praise be glorified, by His saying they destroy their homes the Banu Nadir of the Jews, and that they destroy their dwellings, and that is because they used to look at the wood in what was mentioned in their homes that they liked, or the column or the door, and they would remove that from it with their own hands and the hands of the believers. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers
, they began to destroy them from their interiors, and the believers began to destroy them from their exteriors.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said:
m: When they made peace with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would not take a piece of wood that pleased them, and that was its destruction. Qatada said: The Muslims would destroy what was near them on the outside, and the Jews would destroy it on the inside.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, who said:
m: They carried from their wealth, meaning Banu Nadir, what camels could carry. A man among them would demolish his house from the top of its door, and place it on the back of his camel and set off with it. He said: That is what His statement means: They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. That is their demolishing their houses from the top of their doors when they carried them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty,
h
They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers
, he said: These are the Banu Nadir, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them for what the camels carried, but they began to pull out the pegs and destroy their homes.

x: Others said: It was said thus because they were destroying their homes in order to rebuild what the Muslims had destroyed of their fortresses.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father,
m: on the authority of

x: God Almighty says: And had it not been that God had decreed and written in the Mother of the Book the expulsion of these Jews from Banu Nadir, which is moving from one place to another, and from one town to another. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And had God not decreed upon them exile
, the people’s departure from one country to another.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And had God not decreed upon them exile

. And exile is their expulsion from their land to another land. He said: And exile is also said to mean flight, and it is said from it: The people fled from their homes, and I expelled them. And His statement:
h
He would have punished them in this world
, God Almighty says,
h
And had God not decreed upon them exile
from their land and homes,
h
He would have punished them in this world

by killing and captivity, but He lifted the punishment from them in this world by killing, and made their punishment in this world exile and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire in addition to the humiliation that befell them in this world by being expelled from their land and homes. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said:
m: The Nadir tribe was from a tribe that had not been subjected to exile in the past, and God had decreed exile for them, and had it not been for that,
h
He would have punished them in this world
with killing and captivity.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman:
m: And had God not decreed exile upon them and had there not been a punishment for them from God
h
He would have punished them in this world
meaning with the sword and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire in addition to that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And had God not decreed upon them exile
h
He would have punished them in this world

, and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had besieged them until he had exhausted all their power, so they gave him what he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on the condition that he spare their blood, expel them from their land and homeland, and send them to Adhraat in Syria, and he gave every three of them a camel and a water skin.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And had God not decreed upon them expulsion, the people of An-Nadir, whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged until he had exhausted all of them, so they gave the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he wanted. Then he mentioned something similar, and added to it: This is the expulsion.

x: And His saying, “
h
That is because they opposed God and His Messenger

.” God, Exalted is He, says: This is what God did to these Jews—expelling them from their homes, casting fear into their hearts through the believers, and preparing for them the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter—because of what they did in this world: opposing God and His Messenger in His commands and prohibitions, and disobeying their Lord regarding what He commanded them, namely following Muḥammad, peace be upon him. “And whoever opposes God—God is severe in punishment.” God, Exalted is He, says: Whoever disobeys God in His commands and prohibitions, God is severe in punishment.
God Almighty says: Whatever types of palm trees you cut down, or whatever you left standing on their roots.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of al-Laynah.
Some of them said: It refers to all types of palm trees except for Ajwa.
Who said that?

c: Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: What you cut down of the palm trees he said: the palm tree.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said
m: regarding this verse,
h
What you cut down of the date palms
or left behind, he said: The date palm is the date palm smaller than the Ajwa date.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman,
m: regarding his statement, What you cut down of soft dates, he said: Soft dates are the dates that differ from Ajwa dates. He told us about it again and said: From the palm trees.

c: Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
What you cut down of the date palms
, he said: All palm trees except for the Ajwa date.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
What you cut down of the date palms
, and the date palm is what is not dated from the palm trees.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: What you cut from the soft dates refers to all types of palm trees except Ajwa.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: What you cut of the soft dates, he said: the palm tree, not the Ajwa.

x: Others said: All palm trees are soft, including Ajwa and non-Ajwa dates.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: What you cut down of the palm trees, he said: the palm tree.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, What you cut down of palm trees, he said: Date palms. He said: Some of the Muhajireen forbade others from cutting down date palms, and they said: They are only spoils of war for the Muslims, and the revelation of the Qur’an confirms the one who forbade cutting them down, and absolves the one who cut them down from sin, and he only cut them down and left them with His permission.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun,
m: What you cut down of the palm trees, he said: the palm tree.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
What you cut down of the soft palm trees
, he said: The soft palm tree is the palm tree, whether it was Ajwa or other. God said,
h
What you cut down of the soft palm trees
, he said: What they cut down of the palm trees of Nadir when Nadir betrayed them.

x: The Almighty says: And that which God returned to His Messenger from them, meaning from the wealth of Banu Nadir, it is said from it, the thing returned to someone: if it returned to him, and I returned it to him, if I returned it to him. It has been said: He meant by that the wealth of Qurayzah. You did not mobilize against it any horses or camels meaning: you did not place any horses or camels in it, which are the camels. Rather, the Almighty described that which He returned to His Messenger from them as not being mobilized against it with horses, because the Muslims did not encounter war in that, nor were they burdened with it, but the people were with them, and in their country, there was no mobilization of horses or camels in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels

... the verse, he says: You did not cross a valley to it, nor did you travel to it on foot, but rather they were walls of Banu Nadir that God fed His Messenger. It was mentioned to us, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Any village that gives to God and His Messenger, it is for God and His Messenger, and any village that the Muslims conquer by force, a fifth of it is for God and for His Messenger, and whatever remains is spoils of war for whoever fights over it.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels

, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the people of Fadak and villages he named, which I do not remember, while he was besieging another people, so they sent him a peace treaty, and he said,
h
And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels

, meaning: without fighting. al-Zuhri said: So Banu al-Nadir was exclusively for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not conquer it by force, but rather by peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muhajireen, and he did not give the Ansar anything from it except for two men who were in need.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman:
m: And what God bestowed upon His Messenger from them meaning Banu Nadir you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels, but God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels

, he said: Their Lord is mentioning that He gave them victory and sufficed them without a leg or equipment in the case of Qurayzah and Khaybar. What God bestowed upon His Messenger from Qurayzah, He made it for the emigrants of Quraysh.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels

. But God gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things.” He said: God, the Almighty, commanded His Prophet to march against Qurayzah and Nadir, and the Muslims at that time did not have many cavalry or camels. So he made what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taken he judged as he wished. And there were no cavalry or camels at that time to urge upon. He said: And to urge upon means to put down the cavalry, and it was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among that were Khaybar, Fadak, and Arab villages. And God commanded His Messenger to prepare Yanbu’, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to it and took possession of it all.

x: Some people said, why did he not divide it? So God, the Almighty, revealed His excuse, and said, What God bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the
He means by His saying, may He be glorified,
h
what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns
, that God Almighty returned to His Messenger from the money of the polytheists of the towns. Scholars differed about what is meant by this verse in terms of colors.
Some of them said: It means the jizya and the kharaj.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Khalid, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him recited, Zakat is only for the poor and the needy
r
(At-Tawbah 9:60)
, until he reached, Knowing and Wise
r
(At-Tawbah 9:60)
. Then he said, This is for them. Then he said, And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives
r
(Al-Anfal 8:41)

... the verse. Then he said, This verse is for them. Then he recited, What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns until he reached, for the poor and those who have settled in the home and those who came after them. Then he said, This verse includes all Muslims, so there is no one who does not have a right. Then he said, If I live, the shepherd will come to his donkey while he is walking, and his forehead will not sweat over it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Muammar told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
What God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns
, until it reached me that it was the jizya, and the kharaj: a kharaj from the people of the towns.

x: Others said: What is meant by that is the spoils that Muslims take from their enemy among the people of war by fighting by force.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman:
m: Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, it is for God and for the Messenger - whatever the Muslims fight over with horses and camels, and what was conquered by war by force, “it is for God and for the Messenger
h
and for the near of kin

and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer - so that it will not be a circulating share among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.” He said: This is another division of what was taken by war among the Muslims according to what God has placed it upon.

x: Others said: What is meant by that is the spoils that the Muslims rushed to obtain with horses and riders, and were taken by force. They said that the spoils in the early days of Islam were for those whom God named in these verses, not those who spread rumors about them. Then that was abrogated by the verse in Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans

and the needy and the wayfarer, he said: The spoils of war were for these, then that was abrogated in Surat al-Anfal, and He said, And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer (al-Anfal 8:41). This abrogated what was before it in Surat al-Anfal, and a fifth was made for whoever had the spoils in Surat al-Hashr. The spoils of war were divided into five fifths, four fifths for whoever fought over it, and the remaining fifth was divided into five fifths, one fifth for God and for the Messenger, one fifth for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his lifetime, one fifth for the orphans, one fifth for the needy, and one fifth for the wayfarer. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished, Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, allocated these two shares: a share The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his share of his kinship, so they carried it on him in the Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler so that it will not be a circulating share among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty. way of God as charity on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: What he meant by that was what the people of war had agreed to with the Muslims from their money. They said that his statement,
h
Whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the towns is for God and for the Messenger
... the verses, is an explanation of the division of money that God mentioned in the verse before this verse, which is his statement,
h
Whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from them

, you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. This is a statement that some of the later jurists used to say. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the ruling on this verse is different from the ruling on the verse before it. This is because the verse before it is about wealth that God Almighty made for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically and not for anyone else. He did not give anyone a share in it. This is what was reported from Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, sent for me, so I entered upon him. He said: Some households from your people have come and we have ordered a tribute for them, so divide it among them. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, order someone other than me to do that. He said: Take it, O man. While I was like that, his freed slave, Yarfa’, came and said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Zubayr, Uthman, and Sa’d are asking permission. He said: Give them permission. Then he remained for a while, then he came and said: This is Ali and al-Abbas asking permission. He said: Give them permission. When al-Abbas entered, he said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this traitorous, wicked man. They came to dispute over what God had bestowed upon His Messenger from the works of Banu al-Nadir. The people said: Judge between them, O Commander of the Faithful, and relieve each of them of his companion, for their dispute has been prolonged. He said: I ask you by God by whose permission the world stands up. The heavens and the earth. Do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not inherit what we leave behind as charity? They said: He did say that. Then he said to them: Do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that? They said: Yes. He said: Then I will tell you about this booty. God has singled out His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with something that He has not given to anyone else. He said: And
h
whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from them

- you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. So this was specifically for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). By God, he did not keep it without you, nor did he keep it for himself without you. He divided it among you until this money remained. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would spend from it on his family for a year, then he put what remained in the money of God. So if this verse before it went on and mentioned the money that God singled out for His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and did not make anything with anyone else, and this verse was report about the money that God made for various categories, it was known from this that the money that He made for various categories of His creation is not the money that He made specifically for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and He did not make any partner for him. His statement:
h
And for the near of kin

means: And for the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib. And the orphans are the needy among the Muslim children who do not have money. And the needy are those who are in need and that is the question. And the wayfarer are those who are stranded among the travelers, not for disobedience to God Almighty. We have mentioned the narration that came from the people of interpretation in the previous part of our book. And His statement:
h
So that it would not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you
, God Almighty says: And We made
h
what God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns

for these categories, so that that spoils would not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you, one spending it sometimes on his own needs, and another spending it sometimes on the paths of righteousness and ways of goodness, so that they may do that as they wish, but We have established a law concerning it that will not be changed or altered. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, recited it as Kiyala yakun “Dawla” in the accusative case, as I described of the meaning, and that in Yakun there is mention of the spoils, and his saying Dawla is the accusative of the predicate of Yakun. Abu Jaʿfar al-Fareʿ recited it as Kiyala yakun in the nominative case, Dawla in the nominative case, and the predicate is his saying: among the rich among you, and with the damma of the dal of Dawla all the reciters of the regions recited it, except that it was reported from Abu Abd al-Rahman that it was opened.

x: The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed about the meaning of that, if the dal is closed or open, some of the Kufians said: The meaning of that is if the state is opened: and the army will defeat this

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, recited it as Kiyala yakun “Dawla” in the accusative case, as I described of the meaning, and that in Yakun there is mention of the spoils, and his saying Dawla is the accusative of the predicate of Yakun.

Abu Jaʿfar al-Fareʿ recited it as Kiyala yakun in the nominative case, Dawla in the nominative case, and the predicate is his saying: among the rich among you, and with the damma of the dal of Dawla all the reciters of the regions recited it, except that it was reported from Abu Abd al-Rahman that it was opened.

x: God Almighty says: So that what God has bestowed upon His Messenger may not be a circulating share among the rich among you, but may be for the poor emigrants. It was said that what was meant by the emigrants was the emigrants of Quraysh. Mention who said that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, What God bestowed upon His Messenger from Quraiza, he made it for the emigrants from Quraish.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who said:
m: There were some people from the emigrants, one of whom had a house, a wife, a slave, and a camel on which he used to perform Hajj and fight. So God attributed to them that they were poor, and He gave them a share of the zakat.
b.via: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abza

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes… to his statement
h
Those are the truthful

ones. He said: These emigrants left their homes, wealth, families, and clans. They went out for the sake of God and His Messenger, and they chose Islam despite the hardship it entailed, to the point that it was mentioned to us that a man would tie a stone around his stomach to support his back from hunger, and a man would make a hole in the winter, having no other blanket. His statement:
h
Those who were expelled from their homes and their wealth

, and his statement: seek bounty from God and His pleasure, the position of seek is in the accusative case, because it is in the position of a state. His statement: and support God and His Messenger, means: and support the religion of God with which He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement:
h
Those are the truthful
, means: those whose description he described of the poor emigrants are the truthful in what they say.

x: God Almighty says: And those who were established in the home and in faith meaning: They took Madinah as the city of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and built it as homes, and faith in God and His Messenger before them meaning: before the emigrants, they love those who emigrated to them meaning: they love those who left their homes and moved to them from someone other than them, and by that he meant the Ansar who love the emigrants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And those who were established in the home and in faith before them

, he said: The Ansar are a description. Muhammad ibn Amr said: The generosity of their souls. Al-Harith said: The generosity of their souls, based on what was narrated from them about that and their preferring them, and the Ansar did not receive anything from that booty.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And those who were established in the home and in faith before them

love those who emigrated to them and find not in their breasts any need for what they were given. He says: From what they gave to their brothers, this tribe of the Ansar, they embraced Islam in their homes, so they built mosques and the mosque, before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God praised them well for that, and these two groups first in this verse, took their bounty and went at their leisure, and God confirmed their share of the spoils of war.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty, And those who were established in the home and in faith

x: God Almighty says: And those who came after those who had settled in the home and faith before the first emigrants, they say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith’ from the Ansar. What is meant by those who came after them, the emigrants, is that they seek forgiveness for their brothers from the Ansar. His saying:
h
And do not put in our hearts any rancor toward those who have believed
, means resentment and malice. It was said that what was meant by those who came after them was those who converted to Islam after those who had settled in the home.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And those who came after them
, he said: Those who converted to Islam were also described.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Then God mentioned the third group, and said:
h
And those who came after them

say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers,’ until he reached Indeed, You are Kind and Merciful. They were only commanded to seek forgiveness for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were not commanded to curse them. He told us that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, Hatib will enter the neighborhood of Hell. He said: You have lied, for he witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyyah. He told us that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was harsh with a man from the people of Badr. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “How do you know, Umar? Perhaps he witnessed a scene in which God looked down upon his people and called His angels to witness that I am pleased with these servants of Mine, so let them do what they want.” Some of us continued to shrink from the people of Badr, fearing them. Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to say: And to the people of Badr the perished are destroyed. And this group of the Ansar, may God bestow His praise upon them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And do not put in our hearts any hatred toward those who have believed
, he said: Do not make our hearts inherit any hatred toward any of the people of your religion.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, who said:
m: People were of three ranks: the first emigrants, those who followed them in goodness,
h
and those who came after them

, saying, “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.” And the best thing for one to be in this rank. And His saying: For those who believe, ‘Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.’ God Almighty says, informing about what was said by those who came after those who had settled in the home and faith, that they said: Do not put in our hearts any rancor toward any of the people of faith in You, O our Lord. His saying: Indeed, You are Most Kind and Most Merciful means: You are compassionate towards Your creation, and merciful towards those who repent and seek forgiveness for their sins.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Have you not looked with the eye of your heart, O Muhammad, and seen those who are hypocrites? And they are, as mentioned by Abdullah bin Abi Salul, Wadiah and Malik bin Nawfal, Suwaid and Da'is, who sent to Banu Nadir when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, descended upon them for war, saying: Stand firm and resist, for we will not surrender you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you leave, we will leave with you. So they waited for someone to help them, but they did not, and God cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to expel them and refrain from shedding their blood on the condition that they would have whatever their camels carried of their wealth except the ring.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that.
m: He said: Salamah told us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman. Mujahid said about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Have you not seen those who are hypocrites
? Abdullah bin Abi Salul and Rafi’ah bin Tabut said, and Al-Harith said Rafi’ah bin Tabut, and he did not doubt him, and Abdullah bin Nabtal, and Aws bin Qayzi.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: or on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
Have you not seen those who are hypocrites
? meaning Abdullah ibn Abi Salul and his companions, and whoever among them was like them in their conduct. And His saying:
h
They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture
, meaning Banu Nadir.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture
, meaning: Banu Nadir. His saying:
h
If you are expelled
, we will surely go out with you, means:
h
If you are expelled
from your homes and dwellings, and are evacuated from them, we will go out with you, so we will be evacuated from our homes and dwellings with you. And His statement:
h
And we will never obey anyone concerning you

, meaning: We will never obey anyone who asks us to abandon you and not support you, but we will be with you. And if you are fought, we will surely support you, meaning, even if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him fight you, we will surely support you, the people of Nadir, against them. And His statement:
h
And God bears witness that they are liars
means: And God bears witness that these hypocrites who promised Banu Nadir victory over Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are liars in their promise to them of that.

x: God Almighty says: If Banu Nadir are expelled from their homes and banished from them, the hypocrites who promised to expel them from their homes will not leave with them. And if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, fights them, the hypocrites who promised them victory will not aid them. And if the hypocrites aid Banu Nadir, they will turn their backs in defeat from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, fleeing from them. They have abandoned them. Then they will not be aided. He says: Then God will not aid Banu Nadir against Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, but rather He will abandon them.

God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You, O believers, are more feared by the Jews than Banu Nadir from God. He says: They fear them more than they fear God. That is because they are a people who do not understand. God Almighty says: This fear that you have in the hearts of these Jews, which is more feared by them than they fear God, is because they are a people who do not understand the extent of God’s greatness. Therefore, they belittle His sins and do not fear His punishment as much as they fear Him from you.
And His statement:
h
They will not fight you all together except within fortified villages

, God Almighty says: These Jews, Banu Nadir, will not fight you all together except within fortified villages, they will not come out to you in the open, or from behind walls, he says: or from behind partitions. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Medina read it as or from behind walls in the collective sense of walls.

Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it as from behind a wall in the singular sense of the wall. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And His statement:
h
Their violence is severe among themselves
, God Almighty says: The enmity of some of these infidel Jews toward one another is severe. You think they are all, meaning the hypocrites and the People of the Book. He says:
h
You think they are united
and their word is one. But their hearts are diverse, He says: And their hearts are different due to their enmity toward one another. And His statement:
h
That is because they are a people who do not reason

. God Almighty says: This is what I have described to you about the situation of these Jews and hypocrites, and that is the scattering of their desires and their enmity towards one another, because they are a people who do not reason about what is in their good fortune and what is in it for them is loss and deficiency.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns or from behind walls

. Their violence among themselves is severe. You would think they were together, but their hearts were diverse. That is because they are a people who do not use reason.” He said: You will find the people of falsehood differing in their testimony, differing in their desires, differing in their actions, and they are united in enmity toward the people of truth.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
You think they are united
, but their hearts are diverse, he said: The hypocrites’ religion differs from the religion of Nadir.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: You think they are all one, but their hearts are diverse. He said: They are the hypocrites and the People of the Book. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: You think they are all together, but their hearts are diverse. He said: The polytheists and the People of the Book. He mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading and their hearts are more scattered it means: more scattered, i.e. more different.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Medina read it as or from behind walls in the collective sense of walls.
Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read it as from behind a wall in the singular sense of the wall.

x: God Almighty says: The example of these Jews from Banu Nadir and the hypocrites in what God will do to them by inflicting His punishment upon them is like those before them meaning: like their likeness.
The interpreters differed about who was meant by those before them.
Some of them said: What was meant by that was Banu Qaynuqa.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, “
h
Like those who were shortly before them
. They tasted the consequences of their deed,
h
and for them is a painful punishment
.” He means Banu Qaynuqa.

x: Others said: He meant the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Like those who were shortly before them
h
they tasted the evil consequences of their deed

, he said: The infidels of Quraysh. The most correct of the sayings is to say: God Almighty likened these infidels from the People of the Book to what He will make them taste of His punishment through those who came before them from among the disbelievers of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom He destroyed with His wrath, and the matter of Banu Qaynuqa’ and the Battle of Badr, which were before the expulsion of Banu Nadir, and all of those tasted the consequences of their affair, and God Almighty did not specify some of them in representing these with them over others, and everyone tastes the consequences of his affair, so whoever was close to their time before them, they are represented by them in what they meant by the example. His saying,
h
They tasted the evil consequences of their deed
, means that God’s punishment befell them for their disbelief in Him. His statement,
h
And for them is a painful punishment
, means: And for them in the Hereafter, in addition to the humiliation they suffered in this world, is a painful punishment, meaning: painful.

x: And His statement, “
h
Like Satan when he said to man

, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” God Almighty says: The example of these hypocrites who promised the Jews from Nadir victory if they were fought, or to go out with them if they were expelled, and the example of Nadir in their deceiving them by breaking their promise and submitting to them when they were in dire need of them and their support for them, is like the example of Satan who deceived a man and promised him, in return for following him and disbelieving in God, victory when he needed it. So he disbelieved in God, followed him, and obeyed him. Then, when he needed his support, he submitted to him and disavowed him, and said to him, Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds, in supporting you.

The people of interpretation differed as to whether the person about whom God Almighty said, When He said to man, ‘Disbelieve,’ was a specific person, or was he meant as an example of the person to whom Satan did that?
Some of them said: He meant by that a specific person.
Who said that?

c: Khallad bin Aslam narrated to us: An-Nadr bin Shumayl narrated to us: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Nahik say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: A monk worshipped for sixty years, and the devil wanted to kill him but he exhausted him, so he went to a woman and made her insane, and she had brothers. He said to her brothers: Go to this priest so he can treat her. So they brought her. He said: He treated her, and she was with him. One day while he was with her, he was pleased with her, so he went to her and she became pregnant. So he went to her and killed her. Then her brothers came, and the devil said to the monk: I am your companion, you have exhausted me. I did this to you, so obey me and I will save you from what I did to you. Prostrate to me once. So he prostrated to him, and when he prostrated to him, he said: “Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.” This is what God says: “The example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.’” .

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi told me: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud,
m: regarding this verse: “
h
The example of Satan when he says to man

, ‘Disbelieve.’ And when he disbelieves, he says, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” He said: There was a woman who was tending sheep, and she had four brothers. She would go at night to the cell of a monk. The monk went down and committed adultery with her, and she became pregnant. Satan came to him and said to him, ‘Kill her and then bury her, for you are a truthful man who listens to your words.’ So he killed her and buried her. Satan came to her brothers in a dream and said to them, ‘The monk, the owner of the cell, committed adultery with your sister, and when she became pregnant, he killed her and then buried her in such-and-such a place. When morning came, one of them said, ‘By God, I saw a vision last night, and I do not know whether to relate it to you or leave it?’” They said: No, but tell us about it. He said: So he told it. The other said: And by God, I also saw that. They said: This is for no reason. So they went and took back their kingdom from that monk. They came to him and brought him down. Then they went with him. Satan met him and said: I am the one who caused you to fall into this and no one can save you from it but me, so prostrate to me once and I will save you from what I caused you to fall into. So he prostrated to him. When they brought him to their king, he disowned him and was seized and killed.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The example of Satan when he says to man

, ‘Disbelieve’… to And that is the reward of the wrongdoers. Abdullah bin Abbas said: There was a monk from the Children of Israel who worshipped God and worshipped Him well. He was visited from every land and asked about jurisprudence, and he was a scholar. Three brothers had a beautiful sister, one of the most beautiful people. They wanted to travel and it was too much for them to leave her behind, so they began to plot what to do with her. One of them said, Shall I direct you to someone with whom you should leave her? They said, Who is he? He said: A monk of the Children of Israel. If she dies, he will take care of her, and if she lives, he will protect her until you return to him. So they went to him and said: We want to travel, and we do not find anyone more trustworthy or more protective of what he has been entrusted with than you of what he has been entrusted with. If you see that we should keep our sister with you, she is lost and in great pain. If she dies, take care of her, and if she lives, treat her until we return. He said: I will suffice you, God willing. So they went. So he took care of her and treated her until she was healed, and her beauty returned to her. He looked at her and found her pretending. Satan kept tempting Like the example of Satan when he said to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieved, he said, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds." him to have intercourse with her until he had intercourse with her and she became pregnant. Then Satan made him regret it and tempted him to kill her. He said: If you do not kill her, you will be disgraced and your resemblance to the child will be known, so you will have no excuse. So he kept at him until he killed her. When her brothers came, they asked him what he had done. He said: She died, so I buried her. They said: You did well. Then they began to see in a dream, and they were told that the monk had killed her, and that she was under such-and-such a tree. So they went to the tree and found her under it, having been killed. So they went to him and seized him. Then Satan said to him: I made adultery attractive to you, and her killing after adultery, so would you like me to save you? He said: Yes. He said: Will you obey me? He said: Yes. He said: Then prostrate to me once. So he prostrated to him and then he was killed. That is what God said:
h
The example of Satan when he says to man
, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieves, he says, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you.’

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was a worshipper, and he sometimes treated the insane. There was a beautiful woman, but she became insane, so she was brought to him and left with him. He liked her, so he had intercourse with her and she became pregnant. Then Satan came to him and said: If he finds out about this, she will be disgraced, so kill her and bury her in your house. So he killed her and buried her. Then her family came after that some time to ask him, and he said: She died. They did not accuse him because of his righteousness towards them. Then Satan came to them and said: She did not die, but he had intercourse with her, killed her, and buried her in his house in such-and-such a place. Then her family came and said: We do not accuse you. Tell us where you buried her and who was with you. So they found her where he had buried her, and he was seized and imprisoned. Then Satan came to him and said: If you want me to get you out of what you are in so that you can get out of it, then disbelieve in God. So he obeyed Satan and disbelieved in God. So he was seized and killed, and he was exonerated. Satan was with him at that time. He said: I do not know of this verse except that it was revealed about him: “
h
Like Satan when he said to man
, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’”

x: Others said: Rather, he meant all people by that, and they said: This is only a parable given by Al-Nadir regarding the deception of the hypocrites towards them: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Like the example of Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve,’ the common people.

x: God Almighty says: The consequence of the matter of Satan and the human who obeyed him and disbelieved in God was that they would remain in the Fire forever. And that is the reward of the wrongdoers. He says: That is the reward of the Jews of Nadir and the hypocrites who promised them victory. And every disbeliever in God is wronging himself because of his disbelief in Him, that they will remain in the Fire forever. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative of his statement abiding therein.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is accusative as a state, and in the Fire is the predicate. He said: If it were in the speech, the nominative would have been better in abiding. He said: Their saying: If you come twice is not an accusative of anything, rather it is an emphasis on whether you came with it or not, it is the same, except that the Arabs often make it a state if it is in it for emphasis and what is similar to it in other places. He said: Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: In the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: So the outcome of them was that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, he said: And in that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, there is an accusative. He said: I do not desire the nominative even though it is permissible. If you see the verb between two attributes, one of which returns to the place of the other, you put it in the accusative, so this is from that. He said: And similar to it in speech is your saying: I passed by a man carrying his fang, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: And saffron on her collarbones, eastward, with its pearls and its throat Because the collarbones are the clavicles here, so the adjective returns to the name it was placed on. So if the two adjectives differ, the nominative and accusative cases are good. From that is your saying: Abdullah is in the house, desiring you.

Don’t you see that the in that is in the house differs from the fi that is in desire? He said: The proof is that by which the accusative is known from the nominative case, you do not see the other adjective coming before the first. Don’t you see that you say: This is your brother, in his hand is a dirham, holding it? So if you said: This is your brother, holding it, in his hand is a dirham, it would not be permissible. Don’t you see that you say: This is a man standing before Zaid, in his hand is a dirham? So this indicates that the accusative case is not possible if the other is not brought forward, and it indicates the nominative case if the other is easy to bring forward.

evidence.text: Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: In the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: So the outcome of them was that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, he said: And in that they were in the Fire, abiding therein, there is an accusative.

x: And His saying:
h
O you who have believed
, fear God. God Almighty says:
h
O you who have believed
in God and His Oneness, fear God by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. And His statement,
h
And let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow

, means: Let each one of you look to what deeds he has put forth for the Day of Resurrection, whether they are good deeds that will save him or bad deeds that will destroy him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Fear God and let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow
, your Lord has continued to bring the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow, and tomorrow is the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
What you have sent forth for tomorrow
means the Day of Resurrection.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
What you have sent forth for tomorrow
, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and he read the words of God Almighty, And let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow, meaning the Day of Resurrection, good and evil. He said: And yesterday is in this world, and tomorrow is in the Hereafter. And he read, As if it had never prospered yesterday
r
(Yunus 10:24)
, as if it had never existed in this world. His statement:
h
And fear God
means:
h
And fear God

by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins. Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what you do means: God is All-Knowing and All-Aware of your deeds, both good and bad. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for all of them.

x: God Almighty says: And do not be like those who neglected to perform what God has enjoined upon them, so He made them forget themselves. He says: So God made them forget their own portions of good deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: They forgot God, so He made them forget themselves. He said: They forgot the right of God, so He made them forget themselves. He said: Their own share. And His saying, Those are the transgressors, God Almighty says: Those who forgot God are the transgressors, meaning those who went beyond obedience to God to disobey Him.

x: God Almighty says: The people of Hell and the people of Paradise will not be equal. The people of Paradise are the winners, meaning that they will attain what they sought and wanted, and will be saved from what they were warned against.
And His statement,
h
If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain
, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. God Almighty says:
h
If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain

, which was stone, you would have seen it, O Muhammad, humbled. He says: humbled, coming apart from fear of God despite its hardness, out of caution lest it not fulfill the right of God that is required of it in glorifying the Qur’an, and it was sent down upon the son of Adam while he was belittling its right, and turning away from what is in it of lessons and remembrance, as if he had not heard it, as if there was deafness in his ears. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain

, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God ... to His saying, that they might give thought. He said: He says: If I had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it carrying it, it would have split and become humbled from its weight and from fear of God. So God, the Exalted, the Majestic, commanded the people, when He sent down the Qur’an upon them, to take it with intense fear and humility. He said, Thus does God present examples (al-Ra’d 13:17), for the people that perhaps they might give thought.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain

, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God, God excuses the deaf mountain, but He does not excuse the wretched son of Adam. Have you ever seen anyone whose sides have come apart from fear of God? And these examples We present to the people, God the Most High says, and these things We liken to people, and that is His, the Most High, making them aware that the mountains are more reverent towards His right than they are, despite their hardness and solidity. And His saying,
h
Perhaps they will reflect
, means: God sets forth examples for them so that they may reflect upon them, repent, and submit to the truth.

x: God Almighty says: “O people, He from whose fear the mountain splits, He is the One Whom worship and divinity are due only to Him. He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and sees what is in them of what is seen and sensed. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” He says: He is the Most Gracious of this world and the Hereafter, Most Merciful to those who believe in Him.

God Almighty says: He is the One Who is worshipped and none but Him is worthy of worship, the King above whom there is no king, and nothing but beneath Him, the Holy. It is said: He is the Blessed. I have previously explained the meaning of sanctification with evidence, and I have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on it, so there is no need to repeat it.
Mention of the one who said: It refers to Al-Mubarak.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Holy means the Blessed. And his saying “Peace” means: He is the One who saves His creation from His injustice, and it is one of His names.

c: As Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Peace” means God is peace.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah told us,
m: meaning Al-Ataki, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, regarding his statement, “Peace,” he said: He is God. I mentioned the narration previously, and explained its meaning with its supporting evidence, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And his statement, the believer, means by the believer: the one who makes His creation safe from His injustice. Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The believer is one who believes in his statement that it is true.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The believer believes in his statement that it is true.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: The believer he said:
m: The one who believes.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The believer, he said: The believer is the one who believes and is certain. People believed in their Lord, so He called them believers, and the Generous Lord believed in them because of their belief, so He made them believe that He should be called by that name. And his saying the dominant the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation, some of them said: the dominant is the witness.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, the Guardian, he said: the Witness, and he said another time: the Trustworthy.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the Dominant, he said: the Witness.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, the Dominant, he said: God Almighty sent down a book and bore witness to it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Muhaymin means the witness against him.

x: Others said: Al-Muhaymin: the trustworthy.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Al-Muhaymin is the trustworthy.

x: Others said: Al-Muhaymin means the one who believes.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, The Guardian, said: The one who confirms everything that has happened, and he read, And a Guardian over it (al-Ma’idah 5:48). He said: So the Qur’an confirms what came before it of the books, and God confirms everything that has happened about what has passed of this world, what remains, and what has happened about the Hereafter. The first of these sayings was explained correctly in what came before in Surat Al-Ma’idah with the reasons indicating its correctness, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. His saying, The Mighty means the one who is severe He is God, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Giver of Security, the Guardian, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Supreme. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. in his revenge on those who take revenge on his enemies.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the Mighty means in his vengeance when he takes revenge.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Mighty in His vengeance when He takes revenge. His saying, The Compeller, means: He who reforms the affairs of His creation, directing them toward what is best for them. Qatada used to say: He compels His creation to do whatever He wills of His command.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Jabbar means He compels His creation to do as He wills. And his saying the arrogant it was said that he meant that he was arrogant about all evil.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: The arrogant he said:
m: He is arrogant to all evil.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Abu Raja’ told us: A man told me, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, who said:
m: The greatest name of God is God. Have you not heard Him say: “He is God, other than whom there is no god, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. He is God, other than whom there is no god, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Giver of Security, the Guardian, the Exalted in Might, the Compeller, the Majestic. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him.” He says: To sanctify God and to exonerate Him from the association of those who associate others with Him.

x: God Almighty says: He is the worshipped Creator, there is no deity worthy of worship other than Him, and no creator other than Him, the Maker who created creation, and brought them into existence with His power, the Fashioner who created them however He willed, and however He willed. And His statement,
h
To Him belong the best names

, means that God Almighty says: To God belong the best names, and they are these names that God named Himself with, which He mentioned in these two verses. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, meaning: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him and prostrates to Him willingly or unwillingly. And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning: He is the One who is severe in taking revenge on His enemies. The Wise in His management of His creation and directing them toward what is best for them.
Commentary on Sūrat The Gathering (al-Ḥashr). In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

T2 reads: ‘He was killed on the day he was killed while you loved and approved of his killing by the one who killed him.’ T3 reads: ‘He was killed on the day he was killed while you loved and approved of his killing.’ In either case, the report’s wording is problematic. The citation sources read: ‘If you approved of his killing, then you shared in his blood.’ This wording is supported by a report in Tārīkh Dimashq (37/174–178), where ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said: ‘When the day of Ṣiffīn came, my father ʿAmr swore at me, so I went out. By God, I did not increase their numbers, draw a sword for them, stab with a spear, or shoot an arrow.’ He continued: ‘The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me, “Obey your father while he lives and do not disobey him.” So I am with you’—that is, with his father and Muʿāwiyah—‘but I will not fight.’
